title: A Tufte theme for smalldocs
text: This site shows the theme. The text is set in ET Book, a face cut for Edward Tufte’s books, on a paper that is not quite white. The column is narrow, so a line holds about seventy letters and the eye finds the start of the next one. A link is the colour of the text, with a thin rule under it. The theme takes little away from the page and adds less. The navbar has the colour of the paper. The sidebar and the table of contents are small and grey, and the current page is in italic. Switch to the dark mode with the button in the navbar: the paper turns to near black, as in Tufte CSS.

title: A Tufte theme for smalldocs
text: Add the theme to a smalldocs project, and name it in _smalldocs.yml: smalldocs add rahuldave/smalldocs-tufte theme: tufte The guide has the details, and the notes show a listing of posts.

title: A Tufte theme for smalldocs
text: Page What it shows Install Adding the theme, with smalldocs or with Quarto Typography Headings, text, quotations, lists and callouts Figures A figure with a caption, and tables Code Code blocks, inline code and tabs The commonality between science and art is in trying to see profoundly.

title: Code
text: Code is set in Consolas, or the nearest monospace face, a little smaller than the text. Inline code such as len(xs) has no box around it, only its face.

title: Code
text: A block has a faint tint and a thin rule at its left. The colours of the syntax follow Quarto’s, and change with the mode. def sparkline(values: list[float], width: int = 100) -> list[tuple[float, float]]: "The points of a sparkline: x from 0 to width, y from 0 to 1." lo, hi = min(values), max(values) step = width / (len(values) - 1) return [(i * step, (v - lo) / (hi - lo or 1)) for i, v in enumerate(values)]

title: Code
text: print(sum([78, 84, 93]) / 3) smalldocs render example A tab can hold text as well as code.

title: Code
text: -theme: cosmo +theme: tufte

title: Figures
text: A graphic sits in the column of the text, as wide as the text, so that the words and the picture are read together. Its caption is small and in italic. The rainfall of a made-up town, month by month. The line carries the data and nothing else: no grid, no frame, two labels. The figure above has no gridlines and no box. Two labels mark the months that matter, and the reader can find the rest on the line.

title: Figures
text: A table has three rules: a heavy one above, a light one under the header, and a heavy one below. There are no lines between the rows, and the numbers line up on the right. title: Install
text: The theme is one folder, _extensions/tufte/. It holds a stylesheet for each mode, the ET Book fonts, and the same rules written for Quarto.

title: Install
text: smalldocs add rahuldave/smalldocs-tufte This copies the folder into _extensions/tufte/ and notes where it came from. Then name the theme in _smalldocs.yml: theme: tufte In a _quarto.yml, the line goes under smalldocs:, which Quarto ignores: smalldocs: theme: tufte smalldocs themes lists the themes of a project, with the command that fetches each one again.

title: Install
text: quarto add rahuldave/smalldocs-tufte format: tufte-html: toc: true

title: Install
text: Each stylesheet is a whole Bootstrap 5.3 with the Tufte rules after it, as a Bootswatch theme is. So a page that links to tufte.css in place of bootstrap.min.css gets the theme. Keep the et-book folder next to it.

title: Side notes
text: This is a side note. It stands level with the paragraph that cites it, in the same face as the text, a little smaller. In _smalldocs.yml, or in the front matter of one page. Tufte puts his notes beside the text, and not at the foot of the page or the end of the book. The reader sees the note at the moment the text calls for it, and the eye moves a short way across, and back. A footnote in Markdown becomes such a side note when the page sets reference-location: margin. A margin note has no number. It is a remark beside the text, written as a div with the class .column-margin. Margin notes have no numbers. They suit a remark that the reader can skip, such as a definition, a date or a short quotation. A short note can also sit inside a sentence, as a span with the class .aside, Tufte calls these marginalia and it then stands level with its line.

title: Side notes
text: The rainfall of a made-up town, month by month. With fig-cap-location: margin, the caption stands beside the figure. The caption beside a figure leaves the column of the text for the figure alone, and the reader reads the caption and the picture at the same time. A small figure can go in the margin too, with the class .column-margin. A small figure in the margin works as an illustration of the text beside it, the way a book of Tufte’s places small multiples beside the paragraph that discusses them.

title: Side notes
section: A figure as wide as the page
text: The same data across the width of the page, from the text to the edge of the margin. A figure with much detail needs room. In a div with the class .column-page, it runs from the left of the text to the right edge of the margin. The classes .column-body-outset and .column-screen give a little more width, and the whole window. On a phone there is no margin. The notes then follow the paragraph that cites them, and a wide figure takes the width of the text.

title: Typography
text: Tufte’s books set the text in a single face, in a few sizes, with italic for the headings and for emphasis. There is no bold heading and no coloured bar. The hierarchy comes from size and space alone.

title: Typography
text: A second-level heading is in italic and in the normal weight. It has no rule under it; the space above it is enough to start a new part of the page.

title: Typography
text: The third level is smaller, and still in italic. Below it the text goes on in the same size as before, so that a reader moves from the heading to the text with no change of voice.

title: Typography
text: A paragraph has a generous leading, about one and a half times the size of the type. Emphasis is in italic, and strong text is in bold, which the theme keeps for the rare word that must stand out. Numbers such as 1983 and 2006 use lining figures. A list keeps the size of the text. Its items have the same leading as a paragraph. A long item wraps under its own first word, not under the bullet, so that the column keeps a clean left edge. Above all else show the data. A quotation is set in from the left, with no rule beside it.

title: Typography
text: A note has a thin rule at its left in a muted blue, and no tinted box. The title is in italic, the colour is a dark ochre. An important callout uses a deep red. The body of a callout can fold away under its title.

title: The data and the ink
text: Much of the ink in a chart shows nothing: frames, grids, shadows and fills. Take each away in turn, and keep it out when the chart still says the same thing.

title: Small multiples
text: Small multiples repeat one simple chart for each group, with the same scales. The eye then compares the groups at a glance, and the reader learns the frame once and uses it many times.

title: Sparklines
text: A sparkline is a line chart set in the text, about as tall as a capital letter. It shows a trend where the reader needs it, beside the number that it explains.
